title: Imaging of Distal Radius Fractures Using Projection Radiography in Radiological Diagnostics: Technical Outcome, Clinical Results, Complications, and Economic Implications.
summary:
It aims to show how well the X-ray examinations worked from a technical standpoint and what medical findings resulted from them. To do this, the number of patients for whom the examination was successful—meaning usable images could be obtained—is evaluated. In addition, the frequency of technical problems and failed examinations is recorded.
Furthermore, it is assessed how well the diagnosis made using contrast-enhanced ultrasound matches the results of other imaging methods that were performed to address the same clinical question.
conditions: Analysis of success, complications, and diagnostic quality of radiographic examinations in comparison.

interventions.name: This is a retrospective collection of data from patients who have already been treated, followed by analysis in anonymized form.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients who underwent one or more radiographic examinations at the Department of Radiology, LMU Klinikum, between January 1, 2005, and March 1, 2025.
Exclusion criteria:
- Missing information on the clinical course.
- Missing image data sets in the PACS.
